narrative.northStar: Le Sentier (documentation site) · Le Roadbook (dashboard, beta)
narrative.overview:
Two surfaces share one palette root (pine, deep pine, lime, stone) and keep separate systems. **Le Sentier** is the MkDocs documentation and marketing site (Sora/Inter, photographic hero) and governs every section's first part. **Le Roadbook** is the local dashboard (`web/index.html`, `web/chat.html`, installable PWA), the default dashboard surface since v1.4 behind `[data-design="roadbook"]`; the former dashboard design is deprecated, reachable through `?design=classic` until v1.5 (then deleted); roadbook rules live in each section under *Dashboard roadbook* and apply only under that attribute. A rule from one surface never binds the other unless stated.

The docs are a trailhead, not a manual. Every screen opens onto the runner's own world: deep pine forest, warm stone, a lime accent like a trail marker catching dawn light. The system earns attention with real mountain photography and a quiet alpine type system, then gets out of the way so the reader acts: install in five minutes. The personality is earned and restrained — one full-bleed photographic moment per landing, generous whitespace, soft ambient shadows, and a single authored motion moment on load. Density is low; confidence is high. The palette is earth-and-forest (deep pine greens, warm stone neutrals, energetic lime), chosen from the use scene: a francophone trail runner at dawn, not a corporate dashboard at noon.

**Creative North Star: "Le Roadbook"** — the dashboard is the athlete's season roadbook: the training block drawn as an elevation profile cut into sections, ending at the race finish flag, and each day an aid-station sheet. Laminated sheets lie on stone by day and on deep pine in the morning dark; ink is pine; lime marks only "vous êtes ici" and the one primary action.

The personality is **operational and legible at a glance**, for a phone in dim light before a run. Density is medium-high but ruled, not boxed: content sits in rows with hairlines and tabular numerals, never in stat tiles or ring gauges. Barlow Condensed carries headings, verdicts and numbers like the lettering of a race barrier; Inter carries reading text.
keyCharacteristics: Documentation site: Full-bleed photographic hero as the first viewport, with a dark scrim for text legibility.
Documentation site: Earth-and-forest palette: pine greens, warm stone, lime accent.
Documentation site: Sora display type (tight tracking) over Inter body text.
Documentation site: One authored motion moment (hero rise on load), exponential ease-out, reduced-motion respected.
Documentation site: Soft ambient shadows with real offset and blur; never zero-offset halos.
Documentation site: Generous section rhythm (5rem), tight intra-group gaps (1.4rem).
Dashboard roadbook: Season profile ribbon across the top, with week ticks, month marks, section labels, a lime "vous êtes ici" pin and a chequered finish flag.
Dashboard roadbook: Sheet cards with a 2px pine-ruled head; the day's lead sheet carries a solid pine band instead.
Dashboard roadbook: Verdict word at poster size in Barlow Condensed caps, coloured by state and always a word.
Dashboard roadbook: Cut-off rows: label, condensed tabular value, reference, and a state mark that is a shape plus a word.
Dashboard roadbook: Light (stone) and dark (deep pine) schemes are both first-class, following the system preference or an explicit theme.
Dashboard roadbook: One motion moment: the profile unrolls left to right, then the pin drops.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Lime appears on ≤10% of any screen. It marks action (CTAs, step numbers, trust dots) and nothing else; a second accent color is never introduced.

rules.name: The Tinted-Secondary Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is tinted from the surface hue (green-tinted ink on stone, green-tinted gray on dark) — never pure gray, which reads as disabled.

rules.name: The Tight-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Display and headline letter-spacing is negative (-0.02em to -0.03em) and never looser than normal. The alpine character comes from compression, not from spacing out.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only for code, commands, and measurements — never to make a label look technical.

rules.name: The Offset-Only Rule
rules.body: Every shadow carries a vertical offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration, not depth, and is never used.

rules.name: The You-Are-Here Rule
rules.body: Lime appears only as the "vous êtes ici" marker — profile pin and its label, current rail dot, today's dot in week lists, the active tab notch, today's row tint (lime at 7%) and the selected week on the profile — and as the single primary action. A second lime surface on a screen is a defect.

rules.name: The Word-and-Shape Rule
rules.body: State is never colour alone: every state carries a word ("dans la cible", "à surveiller", "hors cible", "pas de mesure") and a shape (filled circle, triangle, diamond, dash). The verdict colour sits on a verdict word.

rules.name: The Condensed-Caps Rule
rules.body: On the roadbook, uppercase condensed text takes positive tracking (0.01em to 0.08em, wider as it gets smaller) and every number that can be compared is tabular. The docs site's Tight-Tracking Rule governs Sora only.

dos: Do open with the full-bleed photographic hero — the mountain is the promise.
Do use lime only for action: CTAs, step numbers, trust dots.
Do keep display tracking tight (-0.02em to -0.03em) and body measure at 65–75ch in docs.
Do give every shadow an offset and a blur.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling the hero rise.
Do keep lime for "vous êtes ici" and the single primary action; every other emphasis is pine, ink or a state ink.
Do give every state a shape and a word as well as a colour.
Do set comparable numbers in Barlow Condensed with tabular numerals and units in a smaller faint size.
Do pass computed positions through `data-vars` and the CSSOM; the CSP (`style-src 'self'`) refuses inline style attributes.
Do keep every roadbook rule under `[data-design="roadbook"]` so the deprecated classic design (until v1.5) is untouched without the attribute.
Do keep the profile unroll and pin drop as the only motion, removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't add a second accent color; lime is the only one.
Don't use pure gray for secondary text — tint it from the surface hue.
Don't use JetBrains Mono outside code, commands, and data.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use gradient text, glass-as-decoration, or zero-offset colored halos.
Don't add more than one authored motion moment; the hero rise is the only one.
Don't lay out readings as a grid of stat tiles or ring gauges; use ruled rows.
Don't convey state by colour alone, and never soften a red verdict or a medical decision visually.
Don't write `style=` attributes in injected markup.
Don't add a second lime surface or a lime fill on anything but the primary action and the "here" marks.
Don't nest a bordered box inside a sheet; divide with a dashed rule instead.
